THE SCRIPT — every word the film says or shows, and the only place copy is authored.

Nine stations, ids fixed: interior · pair · drawing · facts · note · lineage · wall ·
sentence · mark. Components read this file; they never hold a sentence of their own. A
string that reaches the screen without passing through here has no clearance row, and
`capture/verify-copy.mjs` fails the build on it (CLAUDE.md law 1).

THE VOICEOVER IS COPY. The old film was silent, so its text cards carried the whole
argument; here the spoken lines carry it and the screen carries the evidence. Both halves
go through the same gate — `vo[].text` is scanned exactly as `cards[].lines[]` are.

`wall` HAS NO ROW IN EITHER ARRAY, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The sixth station is a wall of
sixty plans and it is deliberately silent: no voiceover, no card, no number. The rasters
are offline-eval output, and B10 forbids presenting that eval as a public benchmark or
putting a score on it, so the only honest treatment is to show the volume and say nothing.
Do not "fix" the gap by writing a line for it.

`cards[].lines` are AUTHORED LINE BREAKS, rendered `nowrap`. The same sentence breaks in
different places at 1080 and at 1920 wide, so a bad break must surface as an overflow
failure rather than reflow silently. Keep the longest line short enough to survive 1080.

Every line here is registered, byte-identically and in backticks, in docs/copy-clearance.md
with the approved source it came from. Change a character here and the gate goes red until
the row changes too — deliberately: the line nobody cleared is the line that slips.

vo.text: This room doesn't exist yet. It began as one sentence, from someone planning a build.
It came out of the drawing underneath. The room you picture is the room you drew.
One plan, dimensioned to the millimetre. Walls that actually close.
Every room reachable. Every area exact. Checked wall by wall.
And where it couldn't get something right, it tells you, in writing, on the drawing.
Refine it by talking to it. Move a wall, resize a room. Every edit is free.
Describe your home. Get a real, dimensioned floor plan.
Pay only when you get a plan worth keeping.

lines: Three bedrooms, open kitchen and living,
Pay only when you get a plan worth keeping.
A concept plan to take to a professional —
